title_en: Letter to the Emperor Constantius on the Sign Seen in Heaven
author: Cyril of Jerusalem
occasion: Cyril writes to report a luminous cross that appeared in the sky over Jerusalem during the days of Pentecost, stretching from Golgotha to the Mount of Olives, and to interpret it as a divine sign favoring the emperor.
argument: Cyril sends his first letter from Jerusalem to the emperor not with flattery but with news of a heavenly vision. He reports that during Pentecost a huge cross of light appeared over Jerusalem, visible to the whole city for hours and brighter than the sun. He presents this as divine confirmation of the Christian faith and of the emperor's piety, following the discovery of the true cross under Constantine. He urges Constantius to take up the Gospel of Matthew and pay closer, repeated attention to its predictive testimonies, especially the sign of the Son of Man, and to take courage with God as his ally. He closes with prayers that God preserve the emperor and his family in peace.

outline.move: Cyril greets Constantius and says he sends not flattering words but news of a heavenly vision, recalling the finding of the cross under Constantine.
He describes the appearance of a huge cross of light over Jerusalem during Pentecost, visible to the whole city and brighter than the sun, and the crowd's united hymning of Christ.
He says the Jerusalem Christians have worshipped God and prayed for the emperor, and he writes to strengthen Constantius's faith and courage, citing Matthew's prophecy of the sign of the Son of Man.

He urges the emperor to study the Gospel of Matthew's predictive testimonies carefully, offers the letter as his first fruits, and closes with prayers for the emperor's preservation, virtue, and peaceful reign.

cast.name: Cyril of Jerusalem
cast.who: Bishop of Jerusalem and author of the letter.

cast.name: Constantius II
source_forms: βασιλεῖ θεοφιλεστάτῳ καὶ εὐσεβεστάτῳ Κωνσταντίῳ Αὐγούστῳ
cast.who: Roman emperor, son of Constantine, to whom the letter is addressed.

cast.name: Constantine I
cast.who: Father of Constantius, during whose reign the wood of the cross was found in Jerusalem.

cast.name: Jesus Christ
source_forms: τοῦ κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ
cast.who: The Lord and Savior, the only-begotten Son of God, whose cross appeared in the vision.

voices.speaker: Jesus (quoted from Matthew)
voices.how_marked: Introduced as the Savior speaking to his apostles in the Gospel according to Matthew, with a direct quotation.

key_terms.sense: The cross of Christ, especially as a triumphant sign or trophy appearing in the sky.
A heavenly sign, specifically the sign of the Son of Man foretold in the Gospel.
A divine vision or sight granted from heaven.
Piety or devout reverence toward God, especially as shown by the emperor.
A trophy or victory monument, used of the cross as the sign of Christ's victory over death.
Only-begotten, a title of Christ as the unique Son of God.
King of all, a title for God as supreme ruler.
The feast of Pentecost, the fifty-day period after Easter during which the vision occurred.
Golgotha, the holy place in Jerusalem where Christ was crucified, one boundary of the vision.
The Mount of Olives, the holy mountain east of Jerusalem, the other boundary of the vision.
First fruits, used metaphorically for Cyril's first letter to the emperor.

scripture: The author cites the Gospel according to Matthew and quotes Matthew 24:30. He refers to the Gospel book itself and to the Savior's predictions recorded in it. Modern citation: Matthew 24:30.
uncertain: The exact year of the vision is not stated in the text; the date May 351 is inferred from historical context.
The precise identity of the 'pagans from elsewhere' who witnessed the event is not specified.

_unresolved_facts.claim: He urges Constantius to take up the Gospel of Matthew and pay closer, repeated attention to its predictive testimonies, especially the sign of the Son of Man
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἥντινα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου θείαν βίβλον συνηθῶς εἰς χεῖρας ἀναλαβών, τὰς περὶ τούτου κειμένας προαγγελτικὰς μαρτυρίας ἐγγράφως εὑρήσεις· ὧν μαλιστά σε, δέσποτα, πυκνοτέρᾳ τῇ μελέτῃ προσέχειν παρακαλῶ, διὰ τὰ λοιπὰ τῶν κατὰ τὴν αὐτόθι γεγραμμένων ἀκολουθίαν
_unresolved_facts.fix: He urges Constantius, since he customarily takes up the divine book of the Gospel, to find the predictive testimonies about this written in it, and especially to pay closer, repeated attention to them, because of the sequence of the remaining things written there which require great reverent observation

_unresolved_facts.claim: and to take courage with God as his ally
_unresolved_facts.fix: and to take courage, filled with all his customary bravery, so that with God himself as ally he may most readily display the trophy of the cross

_unresolved_facts.claim: He urges the emperor to study the Gospel of Matthew's predictive testimonies carefully
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: Ἥντινα τοῦ εὐαγγελίου θείαν βίβλον συνηθῶς εἰς χεῖρας ἀναλαβών
_unresolved_facts.fix: He urges the emperor, since he customarily takes up the divine book of the Gospel, to pay closer attention to its predictive testimonies

_unresolved_facts.claim: Jesus Christ ... whose cross appeared in the vision
_unresolved_facts.source_quote: τοῦ κυρίου καὶ σωτῆρος ἡμῶν Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ, τοῦ μονογενοῦς υἱοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ, τὸ κατὰ τῆς τοῦ θανάτου νίκης τρόπαιον, ὁ μακάριος λέγω σταυρός
_unresolved_facts.fix: Jesus Christ ... the trophy against death, which I call the blessed cross, appeared in the vision
